families.name: Formal Rules & Authority Allocation
families.definition: Formal permissions, obligations, prohibitions, eligibility boundaries, roles, and allocations of decision authority.
families.includes: Include formal rule content, decision rights, discretion, review rights, and property or control rights.
families.exclusions: Exclude informal cultural norms, individual perceived authority, and immediate interpersonal influence.

families.name: Incentives, Sanctions & Payoffs
families.definition: Institutionally specified rewards, costs, benefits, penalties, liability, and contingency structures.
families.includes: Include tax rates, fees, subsidies, sanctions, reward magnitude, sanction graduation, and liability allocation.
families.exclusions: Exclude intrinsic motivation, market prices absent institutional design, and informal social approval.

families.name: Administrative Burden & Procedural Friction
families.definition: Learning, documentation, procedural, timing, compliance, renewal, and channel requirements created by formal systems.
families.includes: Include required steps, forms, delays, deadlines, recertification, and default enrollment rules.
families.exclusions: Exclude physical distance, subjective effort alone, and information complexity not created by institutional procedure.

families.name: Organizational Structure & Work Design
families.definition: Formal organizational configuration, division of labor, hierarchy, formalization, workload, and coordination design.
families.includes: Include centralization, formalization, standardization, specialization, hierarchy, span, departments, role clarity, mandate conflict, and caseload.
families.exclusions: Exclude informal culture, friendship networks, personality, and physical workspace design.

families.name: Monitoring, Enforcement & Accountability
families.definition: Formal monitoring, enforcement, disclosure, performance-control, oversight, surveillance-mandate, and consequence systems.
families.includes: Include audit intensity, sanction certainty, reporting, transparency rules, performance regimes, feedback, oversight, and accountability consequences.
families.exclusions: Exclude technological sensor capability, peer observation, perceived surveillance, and reputational sanctions.

families.name: Participation, Procedural Governance & Redress
families.definition: Formal voice, representation, inclusion, impartial procedure, explanation, appeals, grievance, and self-governance arrangements.
families.includes: Include collective-choice participation, representation, procedural consistency, reason-giving, redress, and local autonomy.
families.exclusions: Exclude felt fairness, cultural democratic values, and informal conflict mediation.

families.name: Resource Distribution, Eligibility & Service Access
families.definition: Formal allocation, rationing, priority, jurisdictional coverage, gatekeeping, and distributional arrangements.
families.includes: Include budget allocation, structural service coverage, quotas, queue rules, geographic allocation, gatekeeping, and distributional inequality.
families.exclusions: Exclude material stocks and distance, subjective scarcity, and interpersonal resource sharing.

families.name: Market, Labor & Transaction Structure
families.definition: Formal economic rules governing exchange, entry, competition, contracting, ownership, procurement, and employment.
families.includes: Include transaction costs, competition, concentration, entry barriers, procurement, contract rules, and employment protections.
families.exclusions: Exclude individual prices or preferences and purely technological platforms.

families.name: Political Power, Rights & Differential Treatment
families.definition: Formal and de facto allocations of political power, legal status, rights, exclusion, segregation, and unequal application.
families.includes: Include political power, discrimination, differential enforcement, segregation, rights deprivation, veto points, censorship, and border controls.
families.exclusions: Exclude personal prejudice, cultural hierarchy norms, and physical separation without institutional production.

families.name: Corruption, Patronage & Institutional Integrity
families.definition: Misuse of formal authority, private-interest capture, patronage, clientelism, bribery opportunity, and integrity safeguards.
families.includes: Include corrupt practice prevalence, patronage allocation, clientelist exchange, procurement transparency, and conflict-of-interest controls.
families.exclusions: Exclude generalized mistrust, informal reciprocity, criminal outcomes, and cultural tolerance of corruption.

families.name: Interorganizational & Multilevel Governance
families.definition: Formal dependencies, overlaps, pressures, and coordination arrangements among organizations and jurisdictions.
families.includes: Include resource dependence, interdependence, jurisdictional overlap, coordination fragmentation, and coercive, mimetic, or professional pressure.
families.exclusions: Exclude social-network ties and information exchange not embedded in formal arrangements.

families.name: Policy Stability & Institutional Change
families.definition: Temporal durability, review, emergency authority, switching cost, precedent, and learning properties of formal systems.
families.includes: Include policy stability, switching costs, emergency powers, sunset clauses, precedent strength, and organizational learning capacity.
families.exclusions: Exclude path dependence and policy feedback when used only as explanatory frameworks or mechanisms.

families.name: State Capacity & Legal-Institutional Quality
families.definition: Institutional ability to raise resources, staff functions, administer territory, enforce law, deliver services, and sustain impartial legal order.
families.includes: Include fiscal, personnel, administrative, analytic, territorial, judicial, and regulatory capacities.
families.exclusions: Exclude physical infrastructure stock, perceived legitimacy or trust, and broad country labels.
